title: Fluctuation Spectra and Response Function of Coupled Atomic and Molecular BECs
abstract: We investigate out-of-equilibrium properties of atomic molecular Bose Einstein condensates coupled through a Feshbach resonance, with the Feshbach coupling and detuning subject to Gaussian white noise. Using a bosonic Josephson junction framework and a Bloch sphere description, we examine the interplay of detuning, coherence, and noise governing the system dynamics. Coupling and detuning noise produce distinct fluctuation spectra, featuring both Feshbach resonant and symmetric off resonant peaks. We characterize the dispersive and absorptive response of the atom dimer system under periodic driving. The atom molecule hybridization at the Feshbach resonance maximizes the linewidth and minimizes both the effective temperature and the phase difference between the driving field and the system. This leads to an optimized power utilization and quality factor.
summary: The paper theoretically examines how coupled atomic and molecular BECs behave when subjected to external noise affecting their coupling strength and detuning. By mapping the system onto a Bloch sphere, the authors calculate fluctuation spectra and response functions. The key finding is that these noisy dynamics reveal optimal control points near the Feshbach resonance, maximizing power transfer efficiency.
main_problem: The study investigates out-of-equilibrium properties of coupled atomic and molecular Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) when the coupling and detuning are subjected to Gaussian white noise.
main_result: Noise significantly enhances diffusive dynamics, and the system exhibits a dynamical resonance where optimal power utilization and quality factor are achieved near the Feshbach resonance.
method: The analysis employs a bosonic Josephson junction framework using a Bloch vector description, calculating fluctuation spectra via drift ($\Gamma$) and diffusion ($D$) matrices derived from linearized stochastic differential equations.
model_or_system: The system consists of coupled atomic (A) and molecular (M) BECs interacting near a Feshbach resonance. The dynamics are modeled using a two-state system mapped onto the Bloch sphere, incorporating noise in both coupling and detuning parameters.
key_observables: Fluctuation spectra ($	ilde{S}_{ii}$), dynamic mobility ($\mu( ar{\omega})$) (real/imaginary parts), effective temperature ($k_B T_i$), and phase difference ($\Phi$).
important_parameters: Feshbach detuning ($\epsilon_b$), Feshbach coupling noise ($\gamma_x$), and detuning noise ($\gamma_z$).
main_assumptions: The A-BEC and M-BEC are treated as single-mode condensates, neglecting spatial fluctuations; noise is modeled as Gaussian white noise.
figures_summary: Figures show the dependence of fluctuation matrix elements ($	ilde{S}_{ii}$) on Feshbach detuning for different noise sources, and plots illustrate dynamic mobility and effective temperature versus detuning.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the Hamiltonian and stochastic dynamics (using Bloch vector representation) to calculating correlation functions using drift/diffusion matrices. It then analyzes the resulting fluctuation spectra and response function under periodic driving, culminating in characterizing resonance conditions near the Feshbach point.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in a highly relevant experimental platform (BECs via Feshbach resonances), providing quantitative tools to understand noise effects on coherence and energy transfer.
